details: For the first time, the annual Jackson Hole Symposium includes cryptocurrencies and stablecoins on its official agenda, highlighting their growing importance in financial discussions. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled to speak, with the symposium focusing on financial innovation and its policy implications. This marks a significant step towards central bank engagement with digital assets.
title: Jackson Hole Symposium Features Crypto & Stablecoins

details: The U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation for July rose to 3.7% year-over-year, surpassing market expectations. This persistent inflation has increased market expectations for a September interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, leading to higher U.S. dollar strength and Treasury yields. This development typically creates a challenging environment for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: US PCE Inflation Exceeds Forecasts, Fuels Rate Hike Concerns

details: The U.S. Treasury's announcement to double buybacks of longer-duration government bonds has eased pressure on long-term yields and contributed to a weaker U.S. dollar. This intervention has been a significant factor in Bitcoin's recent rally, helping to propel its price above $80,000, reaching a three-month high. The policy revived the "debasement trade," increasing investor interest in alternative assets like Bitcoin.
title: US Treasury Bond Buybacks Boost Bitcoin Rally Above $80K

details: Approximately $6.4 billion worth of Bitcoin options are set to expire on August 28, 2026. This substantial expiry event could introduce increased volatility into the cryptocurrency market. The actual impact on Bitcoin's price will depend on various factors, including the distribution of strike prices and hedging activities by market participants.
title: $6.4 Billion Bitcoin Options Expire Today
